title: Roos exactness for finite continuous module bundles on a profinite slice
statement:
Work in the small-site and indexing universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. For a profinite space $P$ (compact Hausdorff and totally disconnected), equip $\operatorname{Prof}/P$ with finite jointly surjective covering families. For a topological commutative ring $T$, write $R_T(Q\xrightarrow{a}P)=C(Q,T)$, with pointwise operations and pullback of continuous functions. Use ordinary internal $R_T$-modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] and their ordinary uncompleted derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $T$ be any topological commutative ring. Products of $R_T$-module sheaves are exact, and the termwise product of any small family of module complexes represents its ordinary derived product [def-weil-category-product]. Let $(M_k,t_k:M_{k+1}\to M_k)_{k\ge1}$ be a strict inverse sequence of $R_T$-modules. Here a finite locally constant bundle on $P$ is a finite disjoint union of products of clopen subsets of $P$ with finite discrete abelian groups, mapping to $P$ by the first projection. Suppose each underlying sheaf is the sheaf of continuous sections of a finite locally constant bundle $E_k\to P$, every transition is induced by a continuous fibrewise additive map over $P$, and the specified $R_T$-actions make these transitions module morphisms. Put $M=\varprojlim_kM_k$, with its induced $R_T$-action. Then the sequence of sheaf modules
$$0\longrightarrow M\longrightarrow\prod_{k\ge1}M_k\xrightarrow{1-s}\prod_{k\ge1}M_k\longrightarrow0$$
is exact, where $(1-s)(x)_k=x_k-t_k(x_{k+1})$. Consequently $M[0]\to\prod_k^DM_k[0]\xrightarrow{1-s}\prod_k^DM_k[0]\to M[1]$ is distinguished. Finite fibre cardinalities and transition images may vary with $k$ and with $p\in P$; no uniform Mittag--Leffler condition, surjectivity of $t_k$, or extremal disconnectedness of $P$ is assumed.

proof.text: Apply lem-sfb-relative-module-stonean-epi to a map of discrete diagrams of module sheaves. On each Stonean test choose a preimage of every component of a given target section. The source limit is computed sectionwise, and Types.isLimitEquivSections assembles the family into a section; compatibility in a discrete diagram is just the identity law. Naturality of lim.map with each projection shows this section maps to the desired target section. Thus lim preserves epimorphisms, and Mathlib hasExactLimitsOfShape_of_preservesEpi gives exact products, including the empty family.

Install the universe-compatible Grothendieck instance and its K-injective resolutions. The already proved general DerivedCategory.Q product-preservation instance in WeilConjectures.Algebra.Homology.DerivedCategory.TowerLimit applies to the exact products just established. Apply isLimitOfPreserves to HomologicalComplex.isLimitConeOfHasLimitEval to obtain the termwise derived-product statement with precisely its actual localized projections. This reuses the source proof of isLimitFanQ rather than reproving its resolution and product transport.

For the tower let t be towerProductShift and let the first arrow have the limit projections as coordinates. The product projection formula for t and naturality of the limit cone show that this first arrow annihilates 1-t. A map into the product killed by 1-t has compatible adjacent coordinates; NatTrans.ofOpSequence extends these to a cone on the whole tower. The limit universal property gives its unique factorization through limit M. This is exactly the already proved general Fan.IsLimit.isLimitKernelForkOneSub in the same source module, giving a kernel fork and hence a monomorphism and exactness.
Apply lem-sfb-relative-finite-bundle-roos-epi to make the second arrow epic. Together with the kernel fork this gives ShortComplex.ShortExact with the stated canonical arrows.

Transport exact products indexed by ULift Nat down to Nat with Discrete.equivalence Equiv.ulift. The degree-zero single-complex functor preserves products, and so does Q by step 2. Transport preservation along singleFunctorsPostcompQIso. Applying isLimitFanMkObjOfIsLimit to the original product cone supplies the derived product fan with the exact singleFunctor images of the original projections.

Use Mathlib ShortComplex.ShortExact.singleδ and singleTriangle_distinguished, the degree-zero corollary of the short-exact-complex triangle, on the short exact complex just obtained. Its first two maps are definitionally the singleFunctor images of the canonical limit inclusion and towerTransitionEndomorphism. Pair this distinguished triangle with the product universal property from step 5; no conjugation or replacement of either arrow is necessary.

proof_origin.place: Lemma 1.2.7 motivates the relative finite-bundle argument. reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NG-60c29dd14 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read all 8 steps, every cited statement, and RTW 2601.07358 Lemma 1.2.7 (p.14). That lemma only motivates the argument (it reduces to an extremally disconnected closed-point space and defers to FS24), so proof_origin=agent is right. Stacks tags 08TC/08YN/08ZU/005C/005D/03CN/03DA/03DB/03CO/0BK6/07KC exist with the cited labels. No new nodes; proof_deps equals the union of uses; the statement matches what the citer relation-hull step 3 uses. Step 1: C(-,T) restricts to the slice; sheafification on the size-convention skeleton feeds the internal/sectionwise module equivalence; forgetting is faithful and exact. Step 2: the clopen-cover sheaf condition gives B(V)=∏B(S_j) (B(∅)=0); det-pe-stonean-projective (3) gives a section of V→S; det-pe-stonean-cover gives the converse. Step 3: product of epis is epi, so products are exact. Step 4: H^q commutes with products; K-injective resolutions plus lem-pc-ringed-space-product-kinjective show the termwise product with its projections is the derived product, for all small families. Step 5: Z_y is a closed equaliser of continuous maps into Hausdorff F_k, hence profinite. Step 6: the backward recursion solves each finite block (checked x_k−t_k x_{k+1}=y_k) and the finite-intersection leaf gives a solution over each q. Step 7: the single cover makes 1−s locally surjective; the sectionwise limit is ker(1−s). Step 8: the SES triangle plus product uniqueness pins the middle arrow. Edge cases: empty P/Q, a point, zero/identity transitions, varying fibre sizes, non-Hausdorff T. Not duplicates: det-pe-products-exact and the replete nodes are for X_proét with epimorphic transitions. The 7 declared tool_uses are accepted as generic black-box tools. Advisory only: the bundle definition is coherent only if the clopen pieces partition P; step 5 reads it that way, and the wording is inherited from NC.
